newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico placing more Cetes for deficit needs - Werner.
newsitem.headline: Mexico placing more Cetes for deficit needs - Werner.

text.p: The increased amount of government treasury bills that Mexico has put on auction in the last two weeks is due to a government deficit rise, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said in a radio interview on Monday.

"The placement of Cetes has increased... in the last two weeks precisely to deal with the increased deficit," Werner said on Radio Red. Mexico bumped up the amount of Cetes on offer for the weekly auction this week to 4.2 billion pesos, from 3.6 billion pesos the week before.
For most of the year the weekly amount had been stuck at 3.0 billion pesos.

Mexico posted a public sector surplus of 18.271 billion pesos in the first six months of the year, but government officials expect to end the year with a deficit. Werner said this implies spending of 34.0 billion pesos, with a good portion going to social security system reforms and increased government spending on projects in the second half.
Werner added that increased savings should help lift any potential upward pressure on interest rates.
"We think there will be an increase in savings that will help meet needs without putting too much pressure on cash needed by the private sector," Werner said.
